public_rationale: The practical observation is supported. A study public before the post documents model-generated code failing a specified task and requiring iterative debugging. That establishes the additional source of errors Marcus describes. The historical rhetoric needs qualification: compiler research had already documented failures on valid programs. This outcome therefore depends on reading 'new era' as the LLM programming workflow, not the first time computing infrastructure failed.
limitations: The evidence establishes that these failures occur, not their prevalence across all LLM programming.
The supporting study is a preprint and was not independently reproduced here.
A literal claim that infrastructure failures began with LLMs would not be supported.
The emotional description is not graded.

our_interpretation: The checkable core is that LLM-based programming can require correcting model-generated failures even when the supplied task requirements are correct.
I read 'new era' as referring to programming through LLM prompts, rather than asserting that earlier computing infrastructure never malfunctioned. This distinction affects the outcome.
'Frightening' expresses an opinion. 'Apparently' expresses uncertainty, not a conditional antecedent.

The observation concerns the publicly documented technical state by 2024-02-15. There is no recurring reporting period for this capability, so the target ends at the post date and leaves the unspecified beginning open.
criteria.support_condition: Documented programming examples available by the post show an LLM producing code that fails checkable task requirements and consequently requires testing or repair, without an identified error in those requirements.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The documented failures are attributable solely to incorrect user requirements, or reliable evidence establishes that the relevant systems consistently implement correct requirements without model-created errors.
